quarterly_data.quarter: Nippon Chemical Industrial annual securities report: FY2026 (06-25-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 (annual securities report): net sales JPY 40,182 million (103.4% of the prior year; up JPY 1,339 million), operating profit JPY 2,415 million (down JPY 926 million), ordinary profit JPY 2,375 million (down JPY 824 million), profit attributable to owners of parent JPY 2,894 million (up JPY 335 million), after extraordinary gains on sale of investment securities of JPY 1,029 million and on sale of fixed assets of JPY 504 million. Management states sales rose because electronic ceramic materials grew sharply, offsetting lower battery materials, phosphine derivatives and phosphorus products; operating profit fell on a time lag in passing battery-material raw-material price swings into selling prices, the loss of the prior year's inventory-writedown reduction effect and the change in sales mix. Segments: Chemicals sales JPY 17,916 million (98.0%), segment profit JPY 1,281 million; Functional Products sales JPY 21,010 million (111.3%; up JPY 2,133 million), segment profit JPY 513 million (down JPY 699 million); Real estate leasing sales JPY 940 million. Production (at selling prices) JPY 34,215 million (98.2%): Chemicals JPY 13,311 million (86.9%), Functional Products JPY 20,904 million (107.0%); orders are not disclosed because the group mainly produces to forecast. Sales by customer location: Japan JPY 34,680 million, Asia JPY 3,751 million, Americas, Europe and other JPY 1,751 million.
quarterly_data.figure: Net sales JPY 40,182 million (103.4%); operating profit JPY 2,415 million; Functional Products sales JPY 21,010 million (111.3%)

quarterly_data.quarter: Nippon Chemical Industrial annual securities report: FY2026 (06-25-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Functional Products segment, year to March 2026 (annual securities report, management's analysis): electronic ceramic materials - barium titanate, the dielectric of multilayer ceramic capacitors, and high-purity barium carbonate, a dielectric material, made by the oxalate and alkoxide methods - posted a large sales increase as automotive and communications applications grew sharply; the company expects long-term demand growth for AI servers and automotive. High-purity electronic materials (mainly high-purity phosphine gas and high-purity red phosphorus for semiconductors) also rose sharply as semiconductor demand recovered, and the company expects demand to grow with the semiconductor market. Battery materials (lithium cobalt oxide cathode active material for lithium-ion batteries) fell sharply on lower resource prices; phosphine derivatives fell sharply as catalyst raw materials for organic synthesis dropped, despite strong growth in overseas catalysts and quantum dots; agrochemical active ingredients rose sharply on a major customer; circuit materials (conductive particles for ACF / ACP) were flat.
quarterly_data.figure: Functional Products sales JPY 21,010 million; segment profit JPY 513 million

quarterly_data.quarter: Nippon Chemical Industrial annual securities report: FY2026 (06-25-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Electronic ceramic materials supply (annual securities report): the large investment at the Tokuyama Plant (Shunan, Yamaguchi) is complete, establishing a stable two-site supply system together with the Fukushima No. 1 Plant; management states demand is recovering in the electronic-components and semiconductor markets after a temporary adjustment, and the company is building a business base for the expected demand growth for electronic components while it keeps studying semiconductor-material investment, watching material-cost trends. Capital expenditure for the year JPY 4,387 million (Chemicals JPY 1,734 million, Functional Products JPY 2,558 million, Real estate leasing JPY 33 million). Significant new facility plan as of the year-end: electronic ceramic materials manufacturing equipment at the Fukushima No. 1 Plant (Koriyama, Fukushima; Functional Products), total JPY 306 million, JPY 297 million already paid, started May 2024, completion planned May 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: Capex JPY 4,387 million; Fukushima No. 1 electronic ceramic materials equipment JPY 306 million, completion May 2026

quarterly_data.quarter: Nippon Chemical Industrial annual securities report: FY2026 (06-25-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Company targets and strategy (annual securities report): the medium-term plan (2024-2026) targets, for its final year (the company's fiscal 2026, the year to March 2027 = FY2027 in this graph's convention; the report shows fiscal 2025 as the year just ended), net sales of JPY 49.0 billion, operating profit of JPY 3.3 billion, EBITDA of JPY 8 billion and ROE of 6%; the 2030 aspiration is operating profit of JPY 6 billion and ROE of 8% (consolidated). In the electronic ceramic materials growth business the company will use the stable supply system strengthened by the completed large investment to build a business base able to meet future demand growth, and is improving development and market response in both materials and manufacturing processes through collaboration with major customers; for semiconductor materials it will scrutinise the timing and scale of investment while watching material costs and the market.
quarterly_data.figure: Medium-term plan final year (company's fiscal 2026 = FY2027) targets: net sales JPY 49.0 billion, operating profit JPY 3.3 billion; 2030: operating profit JPY 6 billion

quarterly_data.quarter: Nippon Chemical Industrial annual securities report: FY2026 (06-25-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Research and development, year to March 2026 (annual securities report): total R&D expense JPY 1,580 million (Chemicals JPY 204 million, Functional Products JPY 1,376 million). In electronic ceramic materials the company is developing high-performance dielectric materials centred on barium titanate for multilayer ceramic capacitors, to meet demand for smaller, lighter and more functional electronic components; other themes include lithium-ion battery cathode materials and small all-solid-state battery materials, metal-coated powders and conductive pastes for anisotropic conductive connection, phosphine-based organic materials and quantum dots for life sciences, negative-thermal-expansion and CO2-absorbing materials.
